- If sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.3) and prices are trending up, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast rise at 2–4% below peak to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish, model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.
- If model consistently underestimates in 30-day horizon, apply a 2–5% upward bias to compensate for mean reversion bias.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.7) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to reflect hidden momentum.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values before adjustment.
